parameters.microscopeOnPlantedImages: set with set_microscope_parameters(beam_energy=200, convergence_angle=10, collection_angle=20); the line scan carries these in its file

valueToIndex.where: hyperspy 2.4.0 (References/exspy-venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/hyperspy)/axes.py:1283-1349, UniformDataAxis.value2index(value, rounding=round), the default rounding; helpers hyperspy/misc/_array_tools.py:457 (round_half_towards_zero) and :535 (round_half_away_from_zero), reached through hyperspy/misc/array_tools.py:42
valueToIndex.rule: q = (value - offset) / scale; index = (1/1e12) * trunc(q * 1e12)  [axes.py:1315-1318: 1 / multiplier * np.trunc(q * multiplier), a MULTIPLY by 1e-12, not a division]; if value >= 0 (positive scale, axes.py:1323-1327): round half TOWARDS zero, i.e. ceil(index - 0.5) for index >= 0 (a half goes DOWN: 289.5 -> 289); otherwise (value < 0): round half AWAY from zero, floor(index + 0.5) (a half goes UP). The sign test is on the ENERGY value, not on the index. Result outside 0 <= index < size raises ValueError (axes.py:1344-1349). The truncation to 12 decimals makes a value within 1e-12 channels of a half-way point count as exactly half-way.

selfCheck.against: HyperSpy's own value2index on every channel energy, every half-way energy, those nudged by +-1e-13 and +-1e-9, and 20000 RNG values

valueRangeToIndices.rule: i1 = value2index(v1) only if low_value < v1 <= high_value, else 0; i2 = value2index(v2) only if high_value > v2 >= low_value, else size - 1 (axes.py:667, 676-679). The threshold search then crops isig[i1:i2] with INTEGERS (end exclusive): channels [i1, i2). With the defaults start 1.0, window 10.0: [value2index(1.0), value2index(11.0)). If v2 is at or above the last channel's energy the crop ends at size - 1, so the last channel is NOT in it. i2 < i1 + 10 raises ValueError (_eels.py:713-714).

isigFloatSlice.where: hyperspy 2.4.0 (References/exspy-venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/hyperspy)/axes.py:401-471 (BaseDataAxis._get_array_slices), stop at :453-466; used by exspy/signals/_eels.py:598 (self.isig[:threshold].integrate1D(-1)) for a number threshold
isigFloatSlice.rule: isig[:theta] has stop = value2index(theta) (the rule above), end EXCLUSIVE, so I_0 is the sum of channels [0, value2index(theta)); the channel nearest theta is not in it. If value2index raises (theta above the last energy) the slice runs to the end (stop = None, axes.py:462-466) and I_0 = I_t; theta below the first energy raises IndexError (axes.py:457-461). theta exactly at the last channel's energy gives stop = size - 1.

perPixelZeroLossSum.rule: NaN threshold gives NaN. Otherwise ind = axis.value2index(threshold) (the same rule; out-of-range RAISES here, it is not caught) and I_0 = data[:ind].sum() when the axis is binned (numpy pairwise sum of the float64 channels [0, ind)); Simpson's rule when not binned (not ported).

totalIntensity.rule: I_t = sum over ALL channels (axis binned); Simpson when unbinned (not ported). With a zero-loss spectrum I_0 = zlp.integrate1D, the sum of that spectrum (_eels.py:808-809).

savitzkyGolay.rule: scipy.signal.savgol_filter(row, window_length=5, polyorder=3, deriv=1, delta=axis.scale) with SciPy's default mode='interp' and axis=-1, applied to the CROPPED rows. The edges are polynomial fits of the first/last window_length points.

gradientDerivative.rule: numpy.gradient(cropped_rows, cropped_axis_values, axis=-1), edge_order=1; the x array is the cropped axis array offset_c + scale * arange(n) with offset_c = axis[min_index], so the spacings differ from scale by a few ulps (numpy's non-uniform formula).

tolAndThreshold.rule: tol = max over pixels of (min over the cropped channels of |derivative|), ONE number for the image (a pixel's threshold depends on every other pixel's data); inflexion = argmax(|derivative| <= tol) per pixel (the FIRST such channel); threshold = cropped_axis_values[inflexion] (offset_c + scale * inflexion, so it can differ from the full axis value by an ulp); inflexion == 0 gives NaN. The channel exSpy then uses is value2index(threshold) = min_index + inflexion, asserted for every pixel here.

ratioAndThickness.rule: t/lambda = log(I_t / I_0). With a density: t/lambda *= iMFP_angular_correction(beam_energy, alpha, beta, density), then lambda = the given mean_free_path or iMFP_Iakoubovskii(density, beam_energy), then t = (t/lambda) * lambda. With a mean_free_path and no density: t = (t/lambda) * lambda, no correction. With neither: relative t/lambda.

estimated.derivative: scipy.signal.savgol_filter(window_length, polynomial_order=3, deriv=1, delta=axis.scale, mode='interp') on the cropped range

stability.meaning: absolute margins in derivative units (counts/eV): marginAtThreshold = tol - |d| at the pinned channel (null for the pixel that defines tol, whose |d| equals tol exactly); marginBeforeThreshold = smallest |d| before the pinned channel minus tol. A pixel is sensitive when a margin is within 2 * epsilonAbs (epsilonAbs = 1e-12 * the largest |d| of the image, a rounding-level perturbation), or when the two largest per-pixel minima are within 2 * epsilonAbs (tolTie) so that which one defines tol is decided by rounding. For a sensitive pixel the pinned channel is decided by rounding of the derivative: a port can differ from it without being wrong.
